 IRS raises 2027 tax brackets, standard deduction
 Katie Bartlett Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:57 PM CST The IRS is raising 2027 federal tax brackets and the standard deduction, while increasing the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit. (Dreamstime) The IRS is raising federal income tax bracket thresholds and increasing the standard deduction for 2027. The changes could reduce some taxpayers' tax bills as income thresholds rise with inflation. 
 The adjustments apply to income earned in 2027 and generally affect tax returns filed in 2028. 
 The standard deduction - the amount taxpayers may subtract from their income before calculating taxable income - will increase to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, up $1,000 from 2026. It will rise to $16,600 for single taxpayers and $24,925 for heads of household. 
 The top federal marginal income tax rate will remain 37%, but it will apply to taxable income above $661,375 for single taxpayers and $793,650 for married couples filing jointly. 
 The Child Tax Credit is also increasing. The maximum credit will rise to $2,300 per child, up $100 from 2026. The maximum refundable portion will increase to $1,800. 
 The maximum Earned Income Tax Credit will rise to $8,496 for eligible taxpayers with three or more qualifying children, up from $8,231 in 2026
